RuntimeError: Function 'LogBackward0' returned nan values in its 0th output.

question: Tap the line that turns the weights into NaN.

explanation.cause: log(softmax(x)) underflows: softmax returns exact zeros and log’s backward divides 0 by 0
explanation.why: Once a logit sits ~104 below the max, float32 softmax rounds its probability to 0. nll_loss sends zero gradient to those classes, and LogBackward computes grad / input = 0/0 = NaN, so the loss is finite but the weights go NaN after optimizer.step(). Clipping can’t fix a NaN norm. Use F.cross_entropy or F.log_softmax.
explanation.tell: Loss was a finite 0.0171 on the step grad_norm went NaN, the logit range had just crossed ~104, and anomaly mode names LogBackward0.

alert.title: Ads pacing: 61% of campaigns spent their daily budget by 12:00

items.value: all clicks; negatives sampled at 10% to halve training time
bid = pCTR × advertiser value per click

question: Why are campaigns burning through their budgets since ctr-v12?
options: Real drift: users clicking less since the v12 launch
Train-serve skew in a feature added in v12
Negative downsampling left v12's pCTR uncalibrated
Label leakage inflating v12's offline AUC

explanation.cause: v12 trained on 10% of negatives, so its probabilities run ~9× high, and bids use them raw
explanation.why: Dropping 90% of non-clicks makes clicks look ten times more common, which lifts every prediction but keeps the ranking, so AUC doesn’t move. Bids multiply pCTR by value, so every bid is ~9× too high and budgets run out by noon. Recalibrate with q = p / (p + (1 − p) / w), w = 0.1, or upweight negatives 10×.
explanation.tell: Online AUC matches offline and CTR is flat, yet mean pCTR ÷ CTR jumped from 1.0 to 9.1, which is what 10% negative sampling does at a 1.1% CTR.

source.title: Google ML Crash Course — Imbalanced datasets: downsampling and upweighting
